blocks.text: AbortController gives a request a stop signal. It is useful when a page no longer needs a slow answer.

Use these examples in a local page in a current browser. APIs involving files, storage, clipboard or location may need HTTPS, a user action or permission. They are shown as code because this site's sandbox limits those features.

blocks.title: Stop a request

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `AbortController` supplies a signal that can stop waiting for an in-progress request. It does not undo remote work already performed.

blocks.text: The request is cancelled if it is still in progress. Its rejection is handled, usually with the name AbortError.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Cancelling a request does not undo work a server has already done. It stops waiting or reading on the client side.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Find the signal passed into fetch.
